The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial distribution and stratigraphic succession of hemiasteroid echinoids in the north Castilian-Cantabrian region are the result of the interaction of the palaeogeographical evolution of the platform with the palaeoecology and palaeogeography of hemiasteroids.

the spatial distribution and the stratigraphic ranges of hemiasteroid spatangoids are controlled by environmental conditions and that the palaeoecology of these echinoids can be used to infer the palaeoenvironment of the platform.
echinoids, and especially hemiasterids, are useful bioindicators for reconstructing the palaeoecology of the Late Cretaceus platforms of Northern Spain, and probably other areas of the world.
